title: Damodar Kund, Junagadh - A Sacred Lake at the Foothills of Girnar
content:
Damodar Kund, Junagadh

Nestled at the base of the sacred Girnar Hills in Junagadh, Gujarat, Damodar Kund is a revered holy lake deeply associated with Hindu mythology and spiritual traditions. Surrounded by serene natural beauty and ancient temples, this sacred pond is believed to have divine powers to cleanse one’s sins and help souls attain liberation. It attracts both pilgrims and nature lovers seeking peace and purity.

According to legend, Damodar Kund is linked to Lord Krishna and his descendant, Lord Sudama. The lake is mentioned in the Skanda Purana, where it is described as a place of great religious importance. Hindus believe that taking a holy dip here brings spiritual merit and frees ancestors’ souls (known as Pitru Tarpan). The site also holds great significance during the Shraddha Paksha when devotees perform rituals to honor their forefathers.

Close to the lake stands the Damodar Hari Temple, dedicated to Lord Krishna, built in traditional Gujarati style with intricate carvings. The peaceful surroundings, chirping birds, and calm waters make it an ideal place for meditation and reflection.

Best Time to Visit

The best time to visit Damodar Kund is from October to February, when the weather is cool and pleasant. Early mornings and evenings provide a more peaceful atmosphere for prayers and photography.

Entry Fee and Timings

  • Entry Fee: Free
  • Timings: 6:00 AM to 7:00 PM (daily)

How to Reach

  • By Road: Damodar Kund is around 3 km from Junagadh city center, easily reachable by auto or taxi.
  • By Train: The nearest railway station is Junagadh Junction, located about 4 km away.
  • By Air: The nearest airport is Rajkot Airport (105 km), well-connected to major cities in Gujarat.
